groups.defect: When sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but callers (Google res.data, HubSpot token object, Zoho Bigin axios .data) expect their library's own shape. Zoho Bigin also passes credentialId where userId is expected.
groups.rationale: All of these report the same mismatch between what refreshOAuthTokens returns and what its callers expect, either at the producer or at a consumer, and one normalization fixes it. The Bigin suggestions also report the credentialId-as-userId bug, which brings in s_c6985ceb through the overlap chain.

groups.defect: GoogleCalendarService saves the whole SafeParseResult wrapper returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse as the credential key, instead of its .data.
groups.rationale: All three describe the same wrapper being persisted as the Google credential key. One is reported from the helper's file and two from the caller.

groups.defect: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys like [z.string().toString()], which create literal property names instead of a catchall. As a result, validation fails or expiry fields get stripped.
groups.rationale: Same broken schema definition at the same lines. Each fix replaces it with catchall, passthrough or record.

groups.defect: In the webhook, symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse can throw and are not caught, giving a 500. s_0d389f33 also reports that a placeholder refresh_token gets saved.
groups.rationale: Both report the unhandled decrypt/parse error at the same lines. s_0d389f33 adds the placeholder refresh_token problem.

groups.defect: encodeOAuthState copies decodeOAuthState: it parses req.query.state and re-stringifies it instead of actually encoding the state.
groups.rationale: Both describe the same wrong implementation of encodeOAuthState.
